_: Subcutaneous adipose tissue (hypodermis): lobules of fat cells in fibrous septa, in two layers split by the fascia superficialis. Optics as a 'generic' layer: lipid + water + capillary blood + carotenoids (spectra: engine/materials/spectra.json and params/chromophores.json). Sources: the project's materials research note GAPS_RESEARCH.md (keys in caps). Materials foundation lane 2026-11-07. v2 (SKIN lane 11-07): mechanics moved into deform; contact, thermal added (fat is internal: its contact is with fascia, skin and muscle).

thickness_mm.src: bulk: per site in params/tissue_depths.json; a sample's own size

f_lipid.src: THOMAS62: E: recalled from Thomas 1962 (adipose ~70-85 % lipid by mass), not re-read; the lipid spectrum is pure lard (VANVEEN)

f_water.src: THOMAS62: E: recalled from Thomas 1962 (adipose water ~10-30 %), not re-read

f_blood.src: JACQ13 Table 3 (Weaver 1989): subcutaneous fat B 0.76 % - sheep / horse, not human

carotene_M.src: PARKER88: total carotenoids 0.34-13.5 ug/g between people (40-fold, diet); geometric middle 2.1 ug/g x 0.92 g/mL / 537 g/mol = 3.6 uM, beta-carotene's spectrum standing for all (E). PER PERSON: the dial that makes fat white or deep yellow

vessel_radius_um.src: blood in fat sits in capillaries and venules in the septa, not spread evenly: the pigment-packaging factor C = (1 - exp(-2 mu_a,bl r)) / (2 mu_a,bl r) (Svaasand 1995 / van Veen 2005) on the blood term; r 12 um E inside LOOK_TARGETS' 10-25 um (no measured mean). The blood fraction 0.76 % itself is confirmed by living human abdomen 0.43-1.87 % (Lanka 2020, LOOK_TARGETS 2)

a_per_cm.src: JACQ13 Table 2, fatty tissue mean of 6 datasets (SD 9.0): mu_s' = a (lambda / 500)^-b

g.src: soft-tissue typical 0.8-0.95 (JACQ13 general); no adipose-specific value found

n.src: MATIATOU21 human fat n = 1.44933 + 4908.37 / lambda^2 at 550 nm (1.474 at 450, 1.461 at 650); dn/dT -3.5e-4 /K (YANINA18)

superficial_layer.v: small, tightly packed lobules in dense vertical septa (retinacula cutis), elongated perpendicular to the skin; tethered to the dermis

deep_layer.v: looser, oblique, widely spaced septa; slides on the deep fascia

lobule_mm.src: PANDEY15 female abdomen cadaver (7 F); the 3 largest lobules per site, biased high; CAPPELLANO18 disagrees on which layer's lobules are larger

membrane.v: fascia superficialis (Scarpa's fascia in the abdomen) between the layers

septa_medium.v: dermis-like collagen (mu_s' 46 /cm at 500 nm) with 3 % blood
septa_medium.src: septa are dense connective tissue carrying the vessels; blood share E

alpha.src: only seen in a cut section sample: a wet, lobulated cut face

kinetic.src: not found: the deep layer slides on the deep fascia over a lubricated loose areolar plane (MARKMAN87, qualitative)

restitution.src: isolated heel pad (a fat pad in septa) energy loss 46.5-65.5 % (AERTS95) -> e = sqrt(1 - loss) 0.59-0.73; low end

resistivity_ohm_m.src: not retrieved (GABRIEL96 fat low-frequency values not in the table read)

collision_thickness_mm.src: an internal layer: a small offset so fat lobules and septa resolve against fascia (E)

response_time_ms.src: GEERLIGS08; SOFTTISSUE M17/M18 breast 2-7 Hz zeta 0.07-0.22 (a fat-dominated mass)

loss_factor_impact.src: from deform.viscoelastic.loss_factor_vs_freq (GRIG17 heel-fat Prony, computed); zeta_pulse = tan_delta(f) / 2 at f = 1 / (2 x contact time): tan delta 0.078 at 250 Hz, 0.275 at 50 Hz, 0.50 at 25 Hz (computed). how a solver uses it: integrate the Prony set (deform.viscoelastic.prony) as internal variables in an implicit step (one exponential update per term per step; stable at any dt) on top of the hyperelastic stress, so a 1-10 ms slap sees the short-time stiffness and loses energy in the 1-10 ms terms; do not use Rayleigh damping fitted to the ~15 Hz wobble: beta-damping gives zeta = beta * omega / 2, so a beta set for zeta 0.15 at 15 Hz (beta 3.2 ms) gives zeta ~5 at 250-500 Hz (a 1-2 ms pulse): over-damped, the slap goes dead. Where only one number fits, use the loss factor at the pulse's frequency f ~ 1 / (2 x contact time), zeta = tan_delta / 2.

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: per region: set by the stack in the skin profile (compliance_layers)

strain_stiffening.src: SOFTTISSUE section 3: E_t = E0 exp(k eps) from R31's two gluteal fat points (upper bound past eps 0.33)

model.src: one-term Ogden is adequate for subcutaneous adipose at any one strain rate (search summary of the dynamic-loading study; LEG19 uses it)

density_kg_m3.src: ICRU44 via NIST (nominal adipose); pure lipid 900 (SIRI, standard constant)

E_kPa_quasistatic.src: COMLEY10 porcine ~1 kPa (1.15 at 10 % strain); small-amplitude storage modulus 1.8 kPa to 100 Hz (COMLEY)

E_kPa_tension_human.src: ALKHOULI13 human subcutaneous, initial / at 30 % strain (strain-stiffening)

E_kPa_in_vivo_compression.src: SOFTTISSUE R31 (16 men, ultrasound + compression; tangent)

shear_kPa.src: params/soft_tissue_constants.json g_fat_kpa (breast fat MRE in vivo, 43 women); GEERLIGS08 porcine 7.5 kPa at 10 rad/s, 37 C (higher frequency)

bulk_kPa.src: K = rho c^2 = 950 x 1450^2 (DUCK90 sound speed; GAPS_RESEARCH.md 2)

poisson.src: bulk modulus ~2.0 GPa (rho c^2, c ~1450 m/s, DUCK90) over shear ~1 kPa

strain_limit.src: soft_tissue_constants.json fat_strain_limit (R31: compression stiffens past it)

ogden_one_term.src: LEG19 Table 1 fat (first-order Ogden adapted from Payne et al. on COMLEY10's porcine compression)

neo_hookean_C10_kPa.src: C10 = G / 2, G 0.82 kPa (breast fat MRE in vivo, TISSUE)

relaxation.v: power law in time and frequency, no single time constant; phase angle independent of frequency and temperature

prony.src: GRIG17 Table 1 average QLV fit (R2 0.84), human cadaveric HEEL fat pad, drop impacts to ~150 /s: the only human adipose impact-rate Prony set found; heel fat is septate and stiffer (C10 0.1 MPa) than trunk fat, so applied here as E; g_inf = 1 - sum g = 0.15; the abstract prints tau3 10 s, Table 1 0.1 s (Table used). Normalised: multiplies the instantaneous hyperelastic stress

loss_factor_vs_freq.src: computed here from the GRIG17 Prony set (tan delta = G''/G' of the normalised relaxation function, linear, small amplitude); E because the set is heel fat. GEERLIGS08 (porcine subcutaneous, shear, <0.1 % strain) instead finds a power law with a phase angle constant over frequency and temperature (value not retrieved): the peak near 10 Hz is the Prony fit's shape, not a measured peak

high_rate_E_kPa.src: keys: strain rate per s. GRIG17 Yeoh C10(rate) = 0.003 exp(0.028 rate) MPa (R2 0.49), E = 6 C10 (initial, incompressible); heel fat, tested to ~150 /s (failures at 1.7-3.4 m/s drops); E for trunk fat

rate_dependence.v: porcine subcutaneous fat in compression: rate-independent up to ~10 /s, strongly rate-dependent above; stress-strain shape the same at every rate, its level scales with the initial modulus; lock-up near 25 % strain; tested 0.002-5700 /s (numbers not retrieved)

loading_history.src: GEERLIGS10 via LANZL22: the shear modulus rose ~10x for loading times 250-1250 s, reversible after ~3 h (sitting-scale, not impact)

loss_vs_freq_measured.src: MITRA24 Table 1: human abdominal subcutaneous tissue (explants, male and female), shear rheometer, 0.5 % strain (linear), 0.04-40 rad/s (0.006-6.4 Hz): G' = G(1) omega^p, R2 > 0.985, G' > G'' throughout (M). tan delta = tan(p pi / 2) for a power-law (constant phase) solid, computed here (D). GEERLIGS08 (porcine subcutaneous, 0.1 % strain) found the phase angle independent of frequency and temperature with a power law, which is what lets the constant carry upward; still, 100-1000 Hz is 2-3 decades past the measured band (extrapolated). NO direct fat measurement at 100-1000 Hz was found (MRE / ultrasound dispersion of fat not retrieved). Replaces nothing: the GRIG17 heel-fat Prony estimate (loss_factor_vs_freq: 0.16 at 100 Hz, 0.022 at 1000 Hz, E) falls off because a 3-term Prony set has no modes faster than 1 ms; the measured trunk fat behaves as a constant-loss solid
loss_vs_freq_measured.method: small-strain oscillatory shear rheometry, power-law fit, extrapolated by the constant-phase law

G_storage_loss_vs_freq_measured_kPa.src: MITRA24 Table 1 power law G' = G(1) omega^p run to these frequencies, G'' = G' tan(p pi / 2), computed here; 1 Hz inside the measured band, 100-1000 Hz extrapolated. Small-strain (0.5 %) values: at impact strains fat stiffens (deform.stiffening, stiffening_large_strain) and strain-stiffens / shear-thins in LAOS (MITRA24)

layer_stiffness.v: superficial stiffer and tethered, deep sliding (from the structure); no measured split

toughness_J_m2.src: not retrieved: Comley & Fleck measured adipose toughness (2009/2010, GAPS COMLEY) - numbers not in hand

stiffening.form: E_t(eps) = E0 * exp(k * (eps - eps_ref)): tangent compressive modulus at engineering strain eps, quasi-static, in vivo, whole layer in place

E0_kPa.src: ISOGAI22 (SOFTTISSUE R31) gluteal fat in vivo, E at 1 N (strain 0.16) 26.1 +/- 19.0 kPa; reads as a tangent (secant would be ~11)

k.src: ISOGAI22 two points: ln(2199 / 26.1) / (0.33 - 0.16); SOFTTISSUE section 3 (integrates to 1.25-1.65x the measured stress rise: an upper bound)

eps_ref.src: ISOGAI22 strain at the 26.1 kPa point

valid_eps.src: ISOGAI22 measured span (2199 +/- 1355 kPa at 0.33, 30 N); no support beyond 0.33

E_at_eps0_kPa.src: the law run back to eps 0: 26.1 * exp(-26.1 * 0.16) = 0.40 kPa; an extrapolation, but it lands inside the 0.4-3 kPa small-strain values (COMLEY10, ALKHOULI13, breast MRE), so the rest and the loaded values are one curve

stiffening.src: ISOGAI22 via SOFTTISSUE R31 / section 3; quasi-static (rate effects: deform.viscoelastic)

stiffening_large_strain.form: Psi = (mu/alpha)(l1^a + l2^a + l3^a - 3) (Calvo-Gallego's normalisation); uniaxial Cauchy stress sigma = mu (l^a - l^(-a/2)), l = 1 - eps (eps = nominal compressive strain); small-strain E = 1.5 mu alpha, G = mu alpha / 2. Elastic response at the loading-ramp rate (0.5-0.7 /s, the rate of a mm/s probe on a cm layer): relaxation during the ramp is already in it, so do not also apply the Prony set to it

mu_kPa.src: CALVO18 Fig 6 (60 %/s ramp to 40 %, one representative specimen), digitised here and fitted (relative least squares, 11 points 0.06-0.40): mu 0.171, alpha 15.0, worst point -20 % at eps 0.06, within 12 % above 0.12; the same curve as replotted in NASERI22 Fig 13 fits mu 0.149, alpha 15.6; adopted 0.16 / 15. Human abdominal SAT, ex vivo

alpha.src: CALVO18 Fig 6 fit as for mu_kPa. CALVO18's own medians (138 specimens, Tables 3/5) give alpha 8.4-8.5 (QLV) / 8.5-9.4 (IVV), but those sit inside a viscoelastic model whose 0.01-0.1 s modes relax ~85 % of the stress during the ramp; as a purely elastic law the ramp curve needs alpha ~15 (alpha fixed at 8.4 misfits it by -53 % at eps 0.40)

sigma_kPa_check.src: the law above evaluated (Cauchy, compression magnitude); measured CALVO18 Fig 6 ramp: 0.25 (0.06) / 0.40 (0.12) / 0.65 (0.18) / 1.4 (0.24) / 2.85 (0.30) / 3.75 (0.33) / 7.85 (0.403) kPa; 0.5 and 0.6 are the law extrapolated

tangent_kPa_check.src: d sigma / d eps of the law (the gluteal exponential tangent for comparison: 26 / 2206 / 13711 / 186000 / 2.5e6 kPa at 0.16 / 0.33 / 0.4 / 0.5 / 0.6)

valid_strain.src: CALVO18: the fitted ramp reaches 40 % (Fig 6, strain level 40 %); the protocol ramps to 50 % (section 2.1.2). 0.4-0.6 is the Ogden law extrapolated (D): a power law in stretch, it stiffens ~5x per 0.1 strain there, not the exponential's ~14x

rate_s.src: CALVO18 ramps at 50, 60, 70 %/s; constants independent of rate across that span (their non-parametric MANOVA)

site.v: human abdomen, deep subcutaneous fat (skin and the top ~5 mm of fat removed), one woman 57 y (DIEAP flap), ex vivo, frozen up to 1 day at -20 C, tested in 37 C saline, unconfined compression between platens, specimens 19 mm across, 5-10 mm tall

mu_kPa.src: CALVO18 Table 5 IVV long-term Ogden mu, medians 0.102 / 0.197 / 0.169 kPa at 50 / 60 / 70 %/s (IQR 0.066-0.162 at 50 %/s); same normalisation

alpha.src: CALVO18 Table 5 IVV alpha medians 8.47 / 9.42 / 9.29; QLV Table 3 alpha 8.49 / 8.36 / 8.44

equilibrium.use: slow or held loads (seconds to minutes: lying, sitting): CALVO18 report ~70 % of the peak relaxed within seconds and >90 % in 15 min; this law gives sigma 0.9-2.2 kPa at 0.4 and 5-15 kPa at 0.6 (extrapolated)

instantaneous_qlv.src: CALVO18 Table 3 QLV medians at 50 %/s (mu 4.78 kPa, IQR 3.26-9.31; 60 %/s 6.53; 70 %/s 4.55), tau fixed in decades by the authors. For a solver that runs QLV (instantaneous hyperelastic x normalised relaxation): this set replaces the ramp-apparent law, never added to it

spread.v: between specimens of the one donor the fitted mu spans an IQR of ~3x (CV of Q3 230-320 %, some abnormally rigid specimens); one donor only, so the spread between people is not measured

stiffening_large_strain.src: CALVO18 (human abdominal SAT compression to 40-50 %); NASERI22 replot. Other candidates weighed: COMLEY12 porcine (locks up near 25 %; porcine stiffer than human, Sun 2020), SOMMER13 human abdominal (biaxial tension and triaxial shear, no compression; parameters not retrieved), SUN21 human abdominal dynamic compression/shear Ogden-QLV (paywalled, parameters not retrieved), ALKHOULI13 tension to 30 % only

stiffening_which.v: Two compression laws for this fat. (1) deform.stiffening (exponential tangent, ISOGAI22): in vivo, gluteal, whole layer in place, measured 0.16-0.33 strain; use it there for the buttock / sitting layer. (2) deform.stiffening_large_strain (one-term Ogden, CALVO18): ex vivo human abdominal fat, measured 0-0.40, extrapolated to 0.6; use it beyond 0.33 at any site, and across the whole range for the abdomen (and other trunk fat without in vivo data). Never run the exponential past 0.33: at 0.5 it gives ~7 MPa where the Ogden law gives 29 kPa. Where both apply (gluteal, 0.16-0.33) the in vivo law is ~4-60x stiffer in tangent (layer in place: septa, fascia, probe) but within 2x in stress at 0.16 (1.0 vs 0.58 kPa); a join that keeps the gluteal law to 0.33 and continues past it with the Ogden tangent scaled to match there is a D choice for the solver, not measured. Rate: the Ogden ramp law already holds the ramp-rate relaxation (0.5-0.7 /s); for held loads use stiffening_large_strain.equilibrium; a QLV solver uses instantaneous_qlv with its own Prony set
stiffening_which.src: compiled from ISOGAI22 and CALVO18 (large-strain lane 11-08); the REMUS24 abdomen indents (relaxed: 3.33 N at 10 mm, 8.40 N at 20 mm, ratio 2.5) are the in vivo check, not yet rerun with this law

v.E_0.4_kPa_rest_in_vivo_extrapolated: deform.stiffening E_at_eps0: the in vivo law at zero strain; use as the rest tangent of the layer
v.E_1_kPa_COMLEY10: porcine, ex vivo, quasi-static (0.002-0.25 /s), small strain (tangent ~10 %): the material at rest; slow loading; deform.E_kPa_quasistatic
v.E_1.6_to_11.7_kPa_ALKHOULI13: human, ex vivo tension: initial (rest) and tangent at 30 % strain
v.G_0.82_kPa_breast_MRE: human breast fat in vivo, MRE (tens of Hz, micrometre amplitude), no precompression: a small-strain DYNAMIC shear modulus at rest, E ~ 3G = 2.5 kPa; deform.shear_kPa
v.G_7.5_kPa_GEERLIGS08: porcine, ex vivo, shear at 10 rad/s, 37 C, < 0.1 % strain: small-strain dynamic, higher (method, lipid state)
v.E_26.1_kPa_ISOGAI22: human gluteal fat in vivo: the TANGENT at 16 % compressive strain (1 N on 576 mm2, ~1.7 kPa), whole layer in place (septa, fascia, probe): a loaded value, not a rest modulus; deform.stiffening E0
v.E_2199_kPa_ISOGAI22: the same, tangent at 33 % strain (30 N): near lock-up
v.E_18_to_1200_kPa_GRIG17: human heel fat, initial modulus vs strain rate 0-150 /s: rate, not strain (deform.viscoelastic.high_rate_E_kPa)
